newsitem.title: USA: Amoco, Va. refinery sees storm worries pass.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Va. refinery sees storm worries pass.

text.p: Amoco Corp's Yorktown refinery said Friday that the danger of damage from hurricane Fran, downgraded to a tropical storm Friday after hitting the Carolina coast, had passed.
"The refinery continues to operate normally at this stage and we don't anticipate any problems from this point," said Gary Shute, a spokesman for Amoco's Yorktown plant.
Amoco halted shipments in July when the first of the season's hurricanes, Bertha, rolled up the U.S. East Coast.
"The supply situation (for crude into and products out of the plant) has been unaffected (by Fran)," said Shute.

Though heavy rain and storm-force winds were expected to move up the eastern seaboard, other major refineries in the area such as Star Enterprise's Delaware City refinery (140,000 bpd), Sun Co's refineries in Philadelphia, Pa. (307,000 bpd) and Marcus Hook, N.J. (175,000 bpd) also weren't expected to suffer any major disruption.
